subject: Clarify which interactions are kept vs destroyed — BrightBank Qs
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question: what exactly do you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)?

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and our InfoSec team are reviewing Redwood's data handling; two quick clarifications before we complete the vendor questionnaire:

1) When a user types a prompt during an interactive session, is the raw user text stored by default anywhere in your hosted offering, or is that discarded immediately?
2) For streamed responses (token-by-token), do you persist interim buffers or only the final generated text?
3) What counts as a "derived artifact" vs an "original request" for retention and deletion purposes?

We'd prefer short concrete examples we can drop into our questionnaire. If you have a sample retention matrix you can attach, that would be ideal.

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Security Operations
BrightBank

Attachment: brightbank_security_questionnaire.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Aug 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: what exactly do you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)?

Priya — thanks for the concise list. I've attached a single-sheet retention matrix that maps typical interactions to our default handling; below are short, actionable answers you can paste into your questionnaire.

Short answers (paste-friendly):
- User prompt (explicit text input): by default stored as a request record for 45 days in hosted; can be configured to 0 days or to never persist for enterprise private deployments.
- Final generated response (finalized completion): stored by default as a derived artifact for 45 days; customers can opt-out of storing final outputs (make them ephemeral).
- Streamed interim tokens (partial outputs while streaming): not persisted as separate records by default — only the final completion is written to the request/response store unless streaming is explicitly captured for debugging with customer consent.
- KV-cache / model internals: never stored in customer-facing logs; ephemeral caches live only in runtime memory and are purged on session end.
- Attachments (files uploaded as prompt context): persisted in the customer's storage bucket per retention policy; listed as artifacts in audit logs.

I'll also call out two edge-cases:
1) Long interactive sessions with incremental saves (e.g., a notebook-style app) — incremental snapshots are treated as new requests unless the customer uses our "no-persistence" flag.
2) Hybrid flows where prompts are augmented server-side (e.g., prompt engineering augmentation): we treat augmented text as a derivative of the original prompt and it follows derived-artifact retention.

See attached: S3_retention_matrix.xlsx — single sheet, row-per-interaction with default TTL and how to request erasure.

Let me know if you want a one-pager formatted for Legal; we can produce a short Q&A doc.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0123

Attachment: S3_retention_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightbank.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: what exactly do you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)?

Thanks Kimberly — that helps. Couple quick follow-ups:

- The 45-day default: is that a hard maximum for hosted accounts or a rolling TTL we can shorten? Our policy requires deletion within 30 days for sensitive assets.
- EU residency: if a BrightBank user is routed to EU region, do retention and erasure endpoints behave the same (i.e., can we trigger account-scoped erasure and be confident data is removed from all replicated stores)?
- Evidence for erasure: what artifact do we get back when we request a delete for a set of requests?

Appreciate if you can flag anything procurement will care about (SLA for erasure requests, proof artifacts).

—Priya

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@brightbank.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Aug 2029 13:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question: what exactly do you keep by default (prompts vs outputs)?

Priya — quick technical notes to complement Kim's answers:

- TTLs are rolling per-customer keys in hosted: the default is 45 days but we support overrides at the account level down to 0 days (immediate purge) with an enterprise plan and documented API flag. Shortening TTL will remove items from the index and schedule background deletion jobs; final physical delete from retained backups may take up to the backup retention window unless a legal hold is in place.

- EU residency: when a customer opts into the EU region, primary data sits in EU region's storage (region-specific buckets). Erasure requests propagate via our control plane to all replicas and we return a signed erasure receipt once the primary and secondary shards confirm deletion. For customers in regulated regimes we can provide an SLA for erasure within an agreed window and include evidence (signed JSON receipts and audit log extracts).

- Streaming buffers: we treat streaming buffers as ephemeral — we do not commit partial tokens to the request store by default. If a customer toggles "capture-stream-debug" for troubleshooting, that creates a capture artifact which is treated as a derived artifact and follows the configured TTL.

- Evidence artifact example: when you call the account /erasure endpoint for a list of request IDs, we return a signed manifest: {"erased_ids": [...], "timestamp": ..., "region": "eu-west-1"} and an audit log snapshot. We can export that manifest to a customer S3 or upload to a secured Drive link.

Happy to set up a 30-min tech call to walk the team through the API and receipts.

-Rishi
